# mutation: would the test notice if the statement were wrong?

A test that passes a formula and also passes a slightly different formula cannot tell them apart. That makes the
evidence weaker than it looks. Mutation tests perturb what was tested and require every perturbation to be
rejected. `scaling_coefficients` shifts each coefficient of the node's scaling formula by ±1.

| Test | What it checks | A pass grants |
|---|---|---|
| [`mutation/scaling_coefficients`](scaling_coefficients.py) | Every ±1 change to a scaling formula's coefficients is rejected. | Tested (faithfulness). |
